subscriptionRefs.label: Anthropic Claude, developer plan
subscriptionRefs.note: Tier aimed at intensive agentic coding

sectors.name: Defence, space, aerospace supply chain
sectors.note: Explicitly inside national cyber-security perimeters in several EU states. Contractual clauses that forbid data leaving the perimeter. Target the subcontractors, not the prime contractors.

sectors.name: Precision mechanics, automation, packaging
sectors.note: The moat is entirely process know-how and unpublished CAD. Most underserved segment.

sectors.name: Pharma and biotech R&D
sectors.note: Pre-patent compounds and clinical data. Long sales cycles, solid budgets.

sectors.name: Legal and industrial property
sectors.note: Strongest driver of all - disclosure before filing destroys novelty - but almost always below the size floor. Works as a consortium or managed multi-tenant service.

sectors.name: Energy and utilities
sectors.note: Often too large; tends toward framework agreements with sovereign clouds.

sectors.name: Banking and insurance
sectors.note: Strong driver, size usually beyond the band. Exception: cooperative banks and niche asset managers.

sectors.name: Private healthcare and diagnostics
sectors.note: Health data. Avoid public sector: slow procurement, unpredictable budgets.

sectors.name: B2B software and SaaS
sectors.note: Weak driver unless their enterprise customers impose clauses. They can do the maths and will pick cloud.

sectors.name: Professional services
sectors.note: Driver almost absent except on critical-infrastructure contracts.

sectors.name: Other / commodity
sectors.note: No governance driver. The comparison is purely economic and cloud wins.
